Netlify’s built-in Continuous Deployment automatically runs your build commands and deploys the result whenever you push to your Git repository.

### Add a custom domain
Purchase domains and manage DNS zones and records right inside of Netlify.

### HTTPS is automatic

### Deploy Previews

### And a lot more!
Netlify includes solutions for forms, identity, and even custom functions powered by AWS Lambda. And all this functionality can be configured directly in your repo.

body: I pushed a couple of commits adjusting the icons and the toggle size.

# PR review

Nothing here blocks the merge. The Field and label id wiring, SSR, the merge order of the Toggle's event handlers, and the deferred cancel check on form reset all check out. Four things matter most:
- **Extra callbacks:** every form submit and reset calls `onVisibleChange(false)`, even when the password is already hidden.
- **Export name:** the `PasswordFieldPreview` name has no precedent in the library and can't easily be changed after release.
- **Where value props live:** value and form props are on Input, while NumberField and OTPField put them on Root.
- **Merge conflicts:** the branch conflicts with master, and error code `100` is already taken there.

I didn't run the tests or check anything in a browser. The Firefox `:active` finding below is unconfirmed.

## Bugs (10)

### 1. 🟠 `onVisibleChange(false)` fires on every submit and reset, even when the password is already hidden

**Location:** `packages/react/src/password-field/root/PasswordFieldRoot.tsx:53`

```tsx
const setVisible = useStableCallback((nextVisible, eventDetails) => {
  onVisibleChange?.(nextVisible, eventDetails);
  if (eventDetails.isCanceled) return;
  setVisibleState(nextVisible);
});
```

The submit and reset listeners in `PasswordFieldInput.tsx:49-59` call `setVisible(false, …)` unconditionally, and `setVisible` doesn't check whether the value actually changes. The callback's JSDoc says it fires "when the password visibility changes". No other Base UI `on*Change` callback fires when nothing changed. With N inputs in one Root, it fires N times.

**Failure scenario:** A user who never reveals their password submits a login form three times. A consumer logging `onVisibleChange` for analytics records three "hidden" events. Every reset adds another one after the timeout.

**Fix:** Add `if (nextVisible === visible) return;` at the top of Root's `setVisible`. The submit listener's `resetTimeout.clear()` then becomes unnecessary, because a late reset callback is a no-op. Add a test for submitting while already hidden.

### 2. 🟠 The `PasswordFieldPreview` export name has no precedent and is effectively permanent

**Location:** `packages/react/src/password-field/index.ts:1`

```ts
export * as PasswordFieldPreview from './index.parts';
```

No export in `packages/react/src/index.ts` has a `Preview` suffix. On master, Menu's FilterProvider marks its preview status with a `[Preview]` tag in the docs only. The flat type exports (`PasswordFieldRootProps`, `PasswordFieldToggleState`, …) have no suffix, so the signal is mixed.

**Failure scenario:** Users copy `import { PasswordFieldPreview as PasswordField }` from the docs. At stabilization, either every import breaks, or a stable API keeps "Preview" in its name forever, next to the unrelated `PreviewCard`.

**Fix:** Export `PasswordField` and mark preview status in the docs, as FilterProvider does. If the team wants a marker in code, agree on a library-wide convention first.

### 3. 🟠 Value and form props sit on Input, the reverse of NumberField and OTPField

**Location:** `packages/react/src/password-field/input/PasswordFieldInput.tsx:83`

NumberField.Root and OTPField.Root own `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange`, `name`, `required`, `form` and `id`, and their Input part is a thin element. PasswordField.Root owns only `visible` and `disabled`. Everything else goes on Input, as with the plain `Input` component.

**Failure scenario:** The obvious next parts are a strength meter, a "passwords match" hint and a caps-lock indicator, and they need the value in Root context. Moving `value` to Root later leaves two valid places to control the value. That can't be undone without a breaking change once the component is stable.

**Fix:** Decide before release:
- Follow the NumberField/OTPField model, with props on Root.
- Or state explicitly that PasswordField is "an Input plus a visibility toggle", and reserve the Root prop names.

### 4. 🟡 The form is captured once at mount, so the `form` attribute is never tracked

**Location:** `packages/react/src/password-field/input/PasswordFieldInput.tsx:40`

```tsx
const form = inputRef.current?.form;
// ...
}, [inputRef, resetTimeout, setVisible]);
```

None of the dependencies ever change, so the effect runs once.

**Failure scenario:** `<PasswordField.Input form={formId} />` where `formId` arrives after an async load, or the target `<form id>` mounts in a later commit (for example a dialog footer). At mount `input.form` is `null`, so no listener is attached. Submitting the real form then leaves the password revealed, which breaks the stated guarantee that "a revealed password never persists after a submission attempt". If `formId` changes later, the old form keeps the listener.

**Fix:** Add `elementProps.form` to the dependencies. Alternatively, listen in the capture phase on `ownerDocument(input)` and check `event.target === input.form` when the event fires.

### 5. 🟡 Form submit and reset behavior needs an explicit decision

**Location:** `packages/react/src/password-field/input/PasswordFieldInput.tsx:56`

```tsx
addEventListener(form, 'submit', (event) => {
  resetTimeout.clear();
  setVisible(false, createChangeEventDetails(REASONS.none, event));
}),
```

Three coupled behaviors:
- **Prevented submits still hide the password.** Base UI `<Form>` renders `noValidate`, so an invalid submit fires `submit` and is then prevented. The password re-hides while the user is being sent back to fix it. With a plain `<form>` and native `required`, an invalid submit never fires, so the password stays visible. The behavior depends on which validation path is used.
- **Opting out is awkward.** Submit and reset both use the `'none'` reason. Cancelling only the submit hide means checking `eventDetails.event.type === 'submit'`, which isn't documented. Switching to a dedicated reason later would change behavior for anyone keying off `'none'`.
- **Reset ignores `defaultVisible`.** A field with `defaultVisible` ends up hidden after reset, while every other control returns to its default.

**Failure scenario:** On an SPA login form that always calls `preventDefault` and shows "wrong password", the password is re-masked after every failed attempt.

**Fix:** Pick one of two directions:
- Defer the hide and skip it when `defaultPrevented` is set, and/or add dedicated `form-submit`/`form-reset` reasons.
- Keep the current behavior, but document it together with the cancel escape hatch.

### 6. 🟡 Error code `100` collides with master, and the branch has merge conflicts

**Location:** `docs/src/error-codes.json:100`

On master, `"100"` is the Combobox `items` error and `"101"` is the `SelectRootPropsContext` error. `git merge-tree` reports conflicts in `docs/src/error-codes.json` and `docs/src/app/(docs)/react/components/page.mdx`.

**Failure scenario:** A careless conflict resolution maps minified code 100 to the wrong message in production.

**Fix:** Rebase and re-run `pnpm extract-error-codes`. The message also lacks the "why it's a problem" part that AGENTS.md requires.

### 7. 🟡 `onMouseDown` `preventDefault` probably suppresses `:active` press feedback in Firefox (needs a browser check)

**Location:** `packages/react/src/password-field/toggle/PasswordFieldToggle.tsx:50`

```tsx
onMouseDown(event) {
  event.preventDefault();
},
```

Gecko doesn't apply `:active` when mousedown's default is prevented. Both hero demos style the press state with `:active` (`index.module.css:108`, Tailwind `active:not-data-disabled:…`). The `preventDefault` also runs for right and middle clicks, and when the input isn't focused, where it gains nothing.

**Failure scenario:** In Firefox, the demo toggle shows no press feedback.

**Fix:** Call `preventDefault()` only when `event.button === 0` and the input is the active element (using `activeElement(ownerDocument(…))`). Or have the demos style on something other than `:active`.

### 8. 🟡 Root and Input have no styling hook for visibility

**Location:** `packages/react/src/password-field/root/PasswordFieldRoot.tsx:13`

```tsx
const stateAttributesMapping = { visible: () => null };
```

Root removes the `data-visible` attribute it would otherwise get for free, and a test locks that in. Input's state has no visibility field, and Toggle calls the same boolean `pressed`.

**Failure scenario:** The demos make Root the visual box (border, focus-within). Styling it by visibility needs `:has(input[type=text])`, and `className={(s) => s.visible …}` on Input or Toggle is a type error.

**Fix:** Emit `data-visible` on Root (drop the mapping and add it to `PasswordFieldRootDataAttributes`), and add `visible` to the Input state. Adding these later is non-breaking, but renaming state later would be breaking.

### 9. 🟡 With more than one Input per Root, `aria-controls` tracks only the last mounted input

**Location:** `packages/react/src/password-field/input/PasswordFieldInput.tsx:36`

`useRegisteredLabelId` writes to a single `inputId` slot and resets it to `undefined` on cleanup without checking which input owns it.

**Failure scenario:** One toggle reveals both "Password" and "Confirm password". `aria-controls` names only one of them. When the confirm input unmounts, `aria-controls` disappears entirely while the first input is still mounted. Each input also adds its own form listeners, which multiplies finding 1.

**Fix:** Either document "one Input per Root", or keep a registry and emit a space-separated `aria-controls`.

### 10. ℹ️ `disabled` on Input doesn't reach the Toggle

**Location:** `packages/react/src/password-field/input/PasswordFieldInput.tsx:73`

**Failure scenario:** `<PasswordField.Input disabled />` leaves the Toggle enabled, and Root has no `data-disabled`. Revealing a disabled value is arguably harmless, but the behavior should be a deliberate, documented choice.

## Tests (5)

### 1. 🟡 "Form wrapped after mount" test proves only a remount

**Location:** `packages/react/src/password-field/input/PasswordFieldInput.test.tsx:115`

Switching `<div>` to `<form>` changes the element type, so the whole Root subtree remounts. The test only repeats the basic reset case.

**Failure scenario:** Bug 4 (the `form` attribute not being tracked) passes this test.

**Fix:** Rename the test. Add one case that switches `form="a"` to `form="b"` with `setProps`, and another where the input sits outside the form and is linked by the `form` attribute.

### 2. 🟡 Submit test doesn't pin the reason, cancellation, the already-hidden case, or reset-then-submit

**Location:** `packages/react/src/password-field/root/PasswordFieldRoot.test.tsx:225`

Gaps in the current test:
- It doesn't assert `reason`, unlike the reset test.
- Cancelling the hide on submit isn't pinned, although the source comment says "a submit always hides" (see Docs 2).
- Reset followed by submit in the same tick, which is the only reason `resetTimeout.clear()` exists, isn't covered.
- The capture-phase `addEventListener` at line 240 duplicates `onSubmit` and is never removed.

**Failure scenario:** Bug 1 and any change to the cancel contract go unnoticed.

**Fix:** Assert the reason. Add a test that submits while hidden and expects no callback, and a cancel-on-submit test.

### 3. 🟡 Cleanup paths are untested

**Location:** `packages/react/src/password-field/toggle/PasswordFieldToggle.test.tsx:73`

Only the case where the input never mounts is covered. Removing the form listeners when the Root unmounts is untested, and so is clearing `aria-controls` when the Input unmounts.

**Failure scenario:** A regression leaves `onVisibleChange` firing for a field that has unmounted, or leaves `aria-controls` pointing at a missing id.

**Fix:** Add both tests.

### 4. 🟡 Root's `data-disabled` and disabled state from Field are never asserted on Root

**Location:** `packages/react/src/password-field/root/PasswordFieldRoot.test.tsx:136`

The input assertion at line 169 would pass even if Root stopped reading Field's disabled state, because `Field.Control` reads it independently.

**Failure scenario:** `state.disabled` stops including `fieldDisabled`, and Root renders without `data-disabled` inside a disabled Field.

**Fix:** Assert `data-disabled` on Root and on Toggle in both disabled tests.

### 5. 🟡 "Forwards the click handler" doesn't check that the toggle still works

**Location:** `packages/react/src/password-field/toggle/PasswordFieldToggle.test.tsx:261`

The test only checks `onClick` call counts.

**Failure scenario:** A merge-order change lets the consumer handler replace the internal one. The test still passes while the toggle stops working.

**Fix:** Also assert `type="text"` after the click. Add a test where `preventBaseUIHandler()` in `onClick` keeps the password hidden.

Minor: `expect(getByRole('button')).toBeInTheDocument()` at `PasswordFieldRoot.test.tsx:26` can never fail and should assert `aria-pressed="false"`. The `onMouseDown` `preventDefault` is only exercised in Chromium; `expect(fireEvent.mouseDown(button)).toBe(false)` would also cover it in JSDOM.

## Simplifications (1)

### 1. 🟡 The input id round-trips through Root state

**Location:** `packages/react/src/password-field/root/PasswordFieldRoot.tsx:51`

```tsx
const [inputId, setInputId] = React.useState<string | undefined>(undefined);
```

Input generates its id and writes it back to Root in a layout effect, only so Toggle can set `aria-controls`. That costs a second render on every mount, two context fields, a setter and a register/unregister effect. It also means server-rendered markup never has `aria-controls`. `NumberFieldRoot.tsx:108` and `OTPFieldRoot` resolve the id on Root instead.

**Failure scenario:** Extra code and an extra render pass on every PasswordField mount, plus the multi-input bug (Bugs 9).

**Fix:** Take `id` on Root, resolve it with `useBaseUiId`, and pass the plain string through context. Input renders `id={ctx.inputId}`. This fits Bugs 3 if props move to Root.

## Docs (3)

### 1. 🟡 The `disabled` prop is missing from the API reference for Toggle and Input

**Location:** `docs/src/app/(docs)/react/components/password-field/types.md:155`

Toggle's props table lists only `nativeButton`, `className`, `style` and `render`. Both `PasswordFieldToggle.tsx:21` and `PasswordFieldInput.tsx:26` read a working `disabled` prop. The standalone `Toggle` declares `disabled` with a JSDoc comment and `@default false`.

**Failure scenario:** Users can't find out from the docs that the Toggle can be disabled on its own.

**Fix:** Declare `disabled` with JSDoc on Toggle (and Input, if it stays), then run `pnpm docs:api`.

### 2. 🟡 Two source comments describe behavior the code doesn't have

**Location:** `packages/react/src/password-field/input/PasswordFieldInput.tsx:38`

```tsx
// Hide the password again when the owning form is reset or submitted. Field handles the
// value reset; the visibility reset is ours.
// ...
// A reset can be canceled by a handler; a submit always hides ...
```

- **"Field handles the value reset":** nothing in `field/` or `form/` listens for `reset`. The browser restores uncontrolled values, and Field's dirty/filled state isn't reset.
- **"A submit always hides":** `onVisibleChange` can cancel it.

**Fix:** Reword both comments to match the actual behavior.

### 3. ℹ️ The docs examples could teach the API more simply

**Location:** `docs/src/app/(docs)/react/components/password-field/page.mdx:43`

- **Icon swap:** the example uses `render={(props, state) => <button type="button" {...props}>…}`. `type="button"` is redundant because `useButton` already sets it. A CSS swap based on `[data-pressed]` would be simpler to teach.
- **Empty toggle:** the Field example renders a toggle with no content.
- **Missing details:** the sentence "hidden again when … submitted" doesn't mention that `onVisibleChange` fires, or that the hide can be cancelled.

## Verdict

**Approve after nits** - no 🔴/🟣. The spurious `onVisibleChange` calls and the export name and prop placement should be settled before release, because they're hard to change later.

---

## Architecture review I looked at how `PasswordField` (at `aa857697e`) fits with the modules it builds on: Field, `Input`, `Toggle` and NumberField. I compared against current `master`. These are suggestions, ranked by how strongly I'd recommend them. | # | Suggestion | Strength | |---|---|---| | 1 | Root resolves the control id once | **Strong** | | 2 | `PasswordField.Input` reuses `Input`'s interface | **Strong** (cheap) | | 3 | Shared module for controlled state with a cancelable change | Worth exploring (follow-up, codebase-wide) | | 4 | Reveal-reset policy sits beside the visibility state | Speculative | --- ### 1. Root resolves the control id once — **Strong** **Files:** `root/PasswordFieldRoot.tsx`, `root/PasswordFieldRootContext.ts`, `input/PasswordFieldInput.tsx:36`, `toggle/PasswordFieldToggle.tsx:46` **Problem:** The id passes through two registration round-trips, one stacked on the other: - the Input pushes its generated id up to `PasswordField.Root` via `useRegisteredLabelId(idProp, setInputId)`; - `Field.Control` then pushes the same id up to `Field.Root` via `useLabelableId`. Neither one knows the final id during the first render. I copied the PR's `password-field/` directory onto current master and rendered `` with a throwaway jsdom test: - **SSR markup:** the toggle has **no `aria-controls`**. The input and the label use Field's id (`_R_0_`). - **After mount:** the input id, the label's `htmlFor`, and `aria-controls` all switch to the PasswordField-generated id (`_r_2_`). So the input's id **changes after hydration**. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant FR as Field.Root participant PR as PasswordField.Root participant I as PasswordField.Input participant FC as Field.Control participant T as PasswordField.Toggle Note over I,T: Before — render 1 (also SSR) I->>FC: id = generated PasswordField id FC-->>FC: renders Field's controlId instead T-->>T: aria-controls absent Note over I,T: layout effects I->>PR: setInputId(PasswordField id) FC->>FR: registerControlId(PasswordField id) Note over I,T: render 2 FC-->>FC: input id flips T-->>T: aria-controls appears ``` **Suggestion:** Have the Root resolve the id once and pass it down, the same way `NumberField.Root` does (`number-field/root/NumberFieldRoot.tsx:108`, `useLabelableId({ id: idProp })`). The steppers there read `aria-controls` straight from context, so it is correct from the first render. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant FR as Field.Root participant PR as PasswordField.Root participant I as PasswordField.Input participant T as PasswordField.Toggle Note over PR: After — render 1 (also SSR) PR->>FR: useLabelableId (Field-aware) PR->>I: context.id PR->>T: context.id I-->>I: id = context.id T-->>T: aria-controls = context.id ``` **What this buys:** - `aria-controls` is present in SSR markup. - The id no longer flips after hydration. - `inputId`/`setInputId` leave the context. - All the id rules live in one module. - The "omits aria-controls until an input is registered" state disappears. **Open question:** `id` is currently a prop on `PasswordField.Input`. It could move to the Root, as NumberField does, or the Input could keep it as an override, as Collapsible does with its seeded fallback panel id plus registration. Since the component is in preview, now is the cheapest time to decide. --- ### 2. `PasswordField.Input` reuses `Input`'s interface — **Strong** (cheap) **Files:** `input/PasswordFieldInput.tsx:83-110` ↔ `input/Input.tsx:19-37`, `input/PasswordFieldInputDataAttributes.ts` ↔ `input/InputDataAttributes.ts` **Problem:** The Input's surface duplicates `Input` line for line: - the props `value`, `defaultValue` and `onValueChange`; - the `ChangeEventReason`/`ChangeEventDetails` aliases; - the seven-entry data-attributes enum. If `Input`'s interface changes, this copy will silently drift. Also, `disabled={rootDisabled || disabledProp}` (`:73`) combines Field's disabled state a second time: `rootDisabled` already includes it, and `Field.Control` merges it again itself (`field/control/FieldControl.tsx:63`). ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph Before I1["Input
props · event types · data attrs"] --> FC1[Field.Control] P1["PasswordField.Input
props · event types · data attrs
(verbatim copy)"] --> FC1 end subgraph After I2["Input interface
(single source)"] --> FC2[Field.Control] P2["PasswordField.Input
= Input interface
+ visibility-owned type
+ password defaults"] -.extends.-> I2 end Before ~~~ After classDef dup stroke:#dc2626,stroke-width:2px; class P1 dup ``` **Suggestion:** Define `PasswordField.Input` as `Input`'s interface plus the only real differences: the `type`, which follows the visibility state, and the password `autoComplete`/`autoCapitalize`/`autoCorrect`/`spellCheck` defaults. Alias the prop and data-attribute types rather than copying them. Before committing to this, check that `pnpm docs:api` still renders the aliased types on the PasswordField page. --- ### 3. Shared module for controlled state with a cancelable change — Worth exploring (follow-up, not blocking) **Files:** `root/PasswordFieldRoot.tsx:42-62`, plus `collapsible/root/useCollapsibleRoot.ts`, `toggle/Toggle.tsx`, `switch/root/SwitchRoot.tsx`, `checkbox/root/CheckboxRoot.tsx` and others (~22 files contain an `isCanceled` check) **Problem:** Each stateful part writes the same steps by hand: `useControlled`, then call `onXChange(next, details)`, then `if (details.isCanceled) return`, then set the state. This PR adds one more copy. Each copy is another place where the cancel check can be forgotten. ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph Before["Before: ~22 hand-written copies"] direction LR C[Collapsible] ~~~ T[Toggle] ~~~ S[Switch] ~~~ CB[Checkbox] ~~~ PF[PasswordField.Root] end subgraph After["After: one module in @base-ui/utils"] M["controlled + onChange + cancel check + stable setter"] M --> C2[Collapsible] & T2[Toggle] & S2[Switch] & PF2[PasswordField.Root] end Before ~~~ After ``` **Suggestion:** Put that sequence in one `@base-ui/utils` module that the callers use. Behaviour that varies between components, such as transition status or extra side effects after the state is set, stays in each caller. This is out of scope for this PR; I'm only noting that PasswordField adds another instance. --- ### 4. Reveal-reset policy sits beside the visibility state — Speculative **Files:** `input/PasswordFieldInput.tsx:40-61`, `root/PasswordFieldRoot.test.tsx` (the form integration tests) **Observation:** The Root owns `visible`, and the Root's tests check that a form reset or submit hides the password. The policy itself, though, is implemented in the Input: the deferred `defaultPrevented` check on reset and the unconditional hide on submit. Both cases call `setVisible(false, …)` with `REASONS.none`, so `onVisibleChange` can only tell them apart by inspecting `eventDetails.event.type`. ```mermaid flowchart LR F([native form]) -- reset / submit --> I[PasswordField.Input] I -- "setVisible(false, reason: none)" --> R["PasswordField.Root

Considered and dropped: reuse Toggle's internals for PasswordField.Toggle `PasswordField.Toggle` repeats these parts of `Toggle`: - `useButton` - `aria-pressed` - the `{ pressed, disabled }` state - `data-pressed`/`data-disabled` Only ~15 lines are shared, though. `Toggle` also reads `ToggleGroupContext`, so a PasswordField placed inside a ToggleGroup or Toolbar would wrongly join the group. `Toggle` also owns its own controlled state.
